title: Use variables to record inventory changes
goal: uses a variable that can be reassigned to save the inventory after each step.
summary: Variables declared by let can be updated. The right side of the equal sign first calculates the result using the current value, and then stores the result into the variable on the left. return gives the result to the place where this code is called.
tasks: is inside the braces of updateStock, starting from the existing stock. First add the inbound quantity received, then subtract the outbound quantity shipped, and update stock at each step.
uses return to return the final inventory. The parameters are all non-negative integers, and the outbound quantity does not exceed the current available inventory.
hint: reads the updated stock during the second calculation. If initialStock is read again, the first storage will be missed.

example.note: Five minutes after the class starts, update the remaining time to 35. classDuration uses const to save the original class duration, and there is no need to reassign it later.
